from.place: the going-down and surjective-spectrum implication in the lower-bound argument

title: Going down and surjective spectrum bound Krull dimension
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that $\varphi$ has the going-down property: whenever $\mathfrak p_1\subseteq\mathfrak p_2$ are prime ideals of $R$ and $\mathfrak q_2$ is a prime ideal of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_2)=\mathfrak p_2$, there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q_1\subseteq\mathfrak q_2$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_1)=\mathfrak p_1$. Assume also that $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, is surjective. Then $\dim R\le\dim S$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Unfold `ringKrullDim` and `Order.krullDim`, then prove the supremum inequality pointwise for an arbitrary finite strict chain `l` of primes of `R`.
Use spectrum surjectivity to choose `Q : PrimeSpectrum S` contracting to `l.last`; this gives `Q.asIdeal.LiesOver l.last.asIdeal` by congruence of `PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal`.

Apply Mathlib theorem `Ideal.exists_ltSeries_of_hasGoingDown` under the algebra structure induced by `φ`. It constructs a strict ideal chain `L` in `S` with the same length as `l`, starting below `Q` and lying over the chain `l`.
The bound `Order.LTSeries.length_le_krullDim L`, rewritten by the equal lengths, gives `l.length ≤ ringKrullDim S`; taking the supremum proves the result, including empty and unbounded cases.

proof_origin.place: Ideal.exists_ltSeries_of_hasGoingDown together with Order.LTSeries.length_le_krullDim; direct proof in the delivered module
